records.ymmt: 1995-2005 | Buick | LeSabre | Custom, Limited, 90th Anniversary, Celebration | 3.8L L36 (Series II/III)
records.title: LeSabre 3800 V6 Lower Intake Manifold (LIM) Gasket Leak
records.howToFix: LIM gasket job is the same: Fel-Pro MS98003T or similar updated design — $400-$800. Replace UIM plenum if cracked, and drain Dex-Cool. Many shops will replace the EGR stovepipe gasket and throttle body gasket while everything is apart.
records.repairItems: Lower intake manifold gasket; inspect/replace upper intake plenum; drain coolant; optional EGR stovepipe and throttle-body gaskets
destinations: Fel-Pro MS98014T intake manifold gasket set
records.reason: The named MS98003T is a 3.1/3.4L application. MS98014T is the verified 3800 gasket. The product does not cover the optional plenum or ancillary gaskets.
records.correction: Replace MS98003T with MS98014T. Narrow verified link scope to 1996-2005; hold 1995 until its exact engine/VIN split is confirmed.

records.ymmt: 1995-2005 | Buick | Park Avenue | Base, Ultra | 3.8L L36 (Series II/III), 3.8L L67 Supercharged
records.title: Park Avenue 3800 V6 Lower Intake Manifold (LIM) Gasket Leak
records.howToFix: Replace LIM gasket with updated Fel-Pro MS98003T (improved metal-reinforced design) — $400-$800 at independent. Replace upper intake plenum at the same time if cracked. Drain Dex-Cool and refill with Zerex G-05 or compatible HOAT. Inspect oil for coolant contamination at every change; milky oil means immediate teardown.
records.repairItems: Lower intake manifold gasket; inspect/replace upper intake plenum; drain/refill coolant; inspect oil contamination
destinations: Fel-Pro MS98014T intake manifold gasket set
1995-2005 Park Avenue 3.8L; confirm naturally aspirated vs supercharged configuration and VIN
records.reason: MS98014T is the correct 3800 lower-intake set; MS98003T is not. The optional upper plenum and coolant choice remain separate decisions.
records.correction: Replace MS98003T with MS98014T. Remove the blanket recommendation to replace Dex-Cool with Zerex G-05 unless supported by the service information for the exact vehicle.

records.ymmt: 2016-2019 | Buick | Cascada | Base, Premium, Sport Touring | 1.6L Turbo SIDI
records.title: Cascada 1.6L Turbo (Opel SIDI) Timing Chain & Carbon Buildup
records.howToFix: Chain kit replacement ~$1,500-$2,500 (parts harder to source than US-built GM engines). Walnut blast intake valves at the same service ($300-$500). Use dexos2 full-synthetic 5W-30 — required spec for European-build engines.
records.repairItems: Timing chain, guides, tensioner and remaining kit hardware; walnut-blast service; dexos2 5W-30
records.reason: Each OEM component has exact Cascada fitment, but these three links are not a complete kit. Walnut blasting is a service, not a product substitute.
records.correction: Label every component as partial. Do not present a turbocharger, scanner, or a single timing component as the complete repair.

records.title: 6T70/6T75 Transmission Wave Plate Failure
records.howToFix: Disassemble and rebuild the transmission with an updated/stronger wave plate, plus replace damaged hard parts and clean out debris; in severe cases a remanufactured unit is installed.
records.repairItems: Updated 3-5-R wave plate/drum repair; damaged hard parts; debris cleanout; possible remanufactured transmission
records.reason: The Sonnax kit addresses the wave-plate/drum failure but does not cover all hard-part damage, converter damage, labor, programming, or debris cleanout.
records.correction: Gate by transmission ID and diagnosis. Route to a transmission specialist; do not imply that buying one kit completes the rebuild.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption / Engine Failure on 3.6L
records.howToFix: Diagnose per GM PIP5084; remedies range from PCV/oil-control updates to, in severe consumption or block-failure cases, engine replacement (around $6,500). Check oil frequently between changes as a stopgap.
records.repairItems: Diagnosis per GM PIP5084; PCV/oil-control updates if applicable; possible engine replacement
records.reason: The remedy ranges from updates to complete engine replacement. No single part can be recommended until the consumption/block failure is diagnosed.
records.correction: Keep commerce off until diagnosis identifies the failed component. A service/dealer locator is appropriate.

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure
records.howToFix: Replace the failed blend-door actuator and recalibrate the HVAC system. Some actuators are easy to reach; others require significant dash disassembly, which drives up labor.
records.repairItems: Failed HVAC actuator at the diagnosed position; HVAC recalibration
destinations: 2008-2013 Enclave; confirm actuator position by VIN
2013-2017 Enclave 3.6L; confirm actuator position by VIN
records.reason: The Enclave has multiple HVAC actuators that are not interchangeable. The failed position must be diagnosed before purchase; recalibration remains a service step.
records.correction: Display a mandatory position/VIN check. Never label either actuator as fitting every HVAC-door location.

records.title: Loss of Power Steering Assist (Pump Wear)
records.howToFix: Replace the power steering pump (and inspect/replace fluid and lines). Covered under GM Special Coverage for 10yr/150k mi on affected vehicles; otherwise replace the pump out of pocket.
records.repairItems: Power-steering pump; inspect fluid and lines; Special Coverage eligibility check
records.reason: Coverage/VIN check comes before retail. The pump link does not include fluid, lines, steering gear work, or labor.
records.correction: Set recallFirst/coverage-first behavior and make the retail pump secondary.

records.ymmt: 2008-2011 | Buick | Enclave | CX, CXL, CXL-1, CXL-2 | all
records.title: Enclave Power Steering Assist Loss — Special Coverage Adjustment 14329
records.howToFix: Confirm Special Coverage 14329 eligibility at any GM/Buick dealer with your VIN. If still within 10 years and 150,000 miles, remedy is free: dealer flushes power-steering system, replaces the PS pump, and installs a new steering-gear valve housing. If out of the coverage window, expect $700-$1,400 for the same job at an independent.
records.repairItems: VIN eligibility; dealer flush; pump; steering-gear valve housing as directed by Special Coverage 14329
records.reason: The How to Fix explicitly calls for VIN-based coverage and a multi-step dealer remedy. A generic pump link would omit the flush and valve-housing work.
records.correction: Use official coverage/dealer routing. Do not place a buy-parts CTA ahead of the VIN check.

records.title: Rear A/C Evaporator Corrosion & Refrigerant Leaks
records.howToFix: Recover the refrigerant, replace the corroded rear evaporator (and rear blower motor if shedding debris) or the leaking line, then evacuate and recharge the system. Confirm leak source with dye/UV before recharging.
records.repairItems: Leak diagnosis with dye/UV; auxiliary evaporator or leaking line; rear blower if debris-damaged; refrigerant recover/evacuate/recharge
destinations: only if auxiliary core leak is confirmed
records.reason: The TSB identifies auxiliary-evaporator corrosion, but the How to Fix also allows a line or blower failure. Refrigerant work requires proper recovery equipment.
records.correction: Require leak-source confirmation before showing the core as the repair. Do not reuse this link for a leaking line or blower failure.

records.title: Stretched/Worn Timing Chain on 3.6L V6
records.howToFix: Replace the timing chains, guides, and tensioners (a full front-of-engine job). If covered under GM Special Coverage #11340C the repair is free up to 10yr/120k mi; otherwise it is an out-of-pocket repair. Keeping oil changes current and using correct-spec oil slows wear.
records.repairItems: Complete timing chains, guides and tensioners; Special Coverage 11340C check; correct oil
destinations: complete kit for verified year/engine split
records.reason: The ACDelco kit is verified for 2009-2013 LLT/VIN D. The 2008 LY7 application is different and remains held.
records.correction: Split 2008 LY7 from 2009-2013 LLT. Flag as overlapping/duplicative with buick-enclave-timing-chain-2008-2012.

records.ymmt: 2008-2012 | Buick | Enclave | CX, CXL, CXL-1, CXL-2, Premium | 3.6L LLT V6
records.title: Enclave 3.6L LLT Timing Chain Stretch + Oil Consumption
records.howToFix: Timing chain replacement ($2,500-$4,500 with 3-row crossover labor premium). Walnut-blast intake valve carbon at the same time ($300-$500). PCV system update per TSB. Some owners refuse the chain job at this mileage and trade — failure can mean total engine replacement ($6,000+).
records.repairItems: Timing-chain repair; intake-valve walnut blast; PCV update; possible engine replacement
records.reason: The product covers only the timing-chain portion. Walnut blasting and PCV updates are separate services, and 2008 is not an LLT application.
records.correction: Correct the 2008 engine designation (LY7, not LLT), hold its part link, and consolidate this duplicate with the broader timing-chain issue.

records.title: Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Shudder
records.howToFix: Per GM bulletin: flush and refill with the specified DEXRON-VI fluid (part 88862156) and reprogram the TCM with a fast-learn relearn. Persistent cases may require torque converter replacement.
records.repairItems: DEXRON-VI fluid exchange; TCM reprogram and fast-learn; possible torque converter
destinations: ACDelco GM OE DEXRON-VI full-synthetic ATF, 1 gallon, 88865618
2014-2020 Enclave; confirm transmission and bulletin procedure
records.reason: The fluid is verified for the full issue span. TCM programming/fast-learn and converter diagnosis are shop procedures, not replaced by the fluid link.
records.correction: Update obsolete/bulk part 88862156 to current retail GM package 88865618 while retaining the DEXRON-VI specification.

records.title: Water Pump Leak / Coolant Loss on 3.6L V6
records.howToFix: Replace the water pump (and thermostat/gasket as needed), then refill and bleed the cooling system. A relatively common, moderate-cost repair on these vehicles.
records.repairItems: Water pump and gasket; thermostat/gasket if diagnosed; coolant refill and bleed
destinations: GM Genuine water-pump kit with gasket 12709178
2008-2017 Enclave issue scope; GM catalog includes these years
records.reason: The GM product is an exact water-pump-with-gasket repair part for the issue span. Thermostat replacement remains conditional.
records.correction: Keep thermostat/gasket as 'as needed' and include the cooling-system bleed step; do not imply the pump covers every coolant leak.

records.ymmt: 2013-2022 | Buick | Encore | Base, Convenience, Leather, Premium, Sport Touring, Preferred, Essence | 1.4L Turbo LUJ/LUV
records.title: Encore 1.4L Turbo (LUJ/LUV) Timing Chain Stretch
records.howToFix: Full chain kit including chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets ($1,200-$2,000). Use dexos1 full-synthetic 5W-30 and stick to 5,000-mile intervals — extended OLM intervals are the dominant cause. Catastrophic chain skip means head rebuild ($3,500+).
records.repairItems: Timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets; dexos1 5W-30 maintenance
records.reason: The kit has verified 2013-2021 1.4L fitment; the issue's 2022 model year remains unverified for this exact product.
records.correction: Hold 2022 rather than stretching the product fitment. Confirm kit contents before claiming every sprocket/guide is included.

records.title: 6T40 Automatic Transmission Hard Shifting, Shudder and Slipping
records.howToFix: Service the transmission with the correct fluid; for shudder, a torque-converter clutch fluid/flush or solenoid replacement may help. Persistent 2-6 slip/flare typically requires valve body/channel-plate cleaning or rebuild. Confirm GM software calibration is current, as updated shift logic addressed some complaints.
records.repairItems: Correct DEXRON-VI fluid service; possible TCC/solenoid; valve body/channel plate; rebuild; software calibration
destinations: ACDelco GM OE DEXRON-VI ATF, 1 quart, 88865601
2013-2018 Encore issue scope; official catalog lists 2013-2022
records.reason: DEXRON-VI is verified, but the remaining fixes depend on whether the fault is converter, solenoid/TEHCM, valve body, calibration, or internal damage.
records.correction: Do not link a solenoid, TEHCM, scanner, or rebuild kit until diagnosis identifies that repair. The fluid link is not a promise that service cures slipping.
